items.design_state: Vacuum-state definition authored; two independent full-text treatments stamped; focused dependency and rendering checks pass.
items.statement:
Let a positive unitary representation of the four-dimensional extended super-Poincare algebra act on a complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, with common invariant product domain $\mathcal D$, translation generators $P^\mu$, supercharges $Q^I_\alpha$, and actual Hilbert adjoints $(Q^I_\alpha)^*$, using metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\sigma^0=I_2$, and natural units $\hbar=c=1$. A **rest-frame ground-state vector** is a vector $\Omega\in\mathcal D$ such that $\|\Omega\|=1$, there is a real number $E_\Omega$ with $P^0\Omega=E_\Omega\Omega$ and $P^j\Omega=0$ for $j=1,2,3$, and

$$\langle P^0\psi,\psi\rangle\ge E_\Omega\|\psi\|^2\qquad(\psi\in D(P^0)).$$

Such a vector is called a **global supersymmetry vacuum state** in the representation. Its vacuum energy is the eigenvalue $E_\Omega$, with units of mass in natural units; it is not an energy density. The vector is **boundary-neutral** when $Z^{IJ}\Omega=0$ and $\bar Z_{IJ}\Omega=0$ for every central generator, **supersymmetry-invariant** when $Q^I_\alpha\Omega=(Q^I_\alpha)^*\Omega=0$ for every $I,\alpha$, and **supersymmetry-noninvariant** when at least one of these vectors is nonzero. These are separate predicates: boundary neutrality does not define supersymmetry invariance. The definition does not assert that any such vector exists or that a constant field configuration is allowed by a separate field-model boundary condition.

items.title: Vacuum energy and global supersymmetry invariance
items.physical_scope: Conditional operator-algebra deduction for an existing rest-frame ground-state vector in an adopted positive unitary representation of the four-dimensional extended super-Poincare algebra. The result identifies zero energy with supercharge invariance; it does not establish vacuum existence, construct a QFT, or infer a nonzero vacuum energy from a field-potential calculation.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and a positive unitary representation of the four-dimensional extended super-Poincare algebra with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\sigma^0=I_2$, natural units $\hbar=c=1$, common invariant product domain $\mathcal D$, and actual Hilbert adjoints $(Q^I_\alpha)^*$. Let $N\ge1$, and let $\Omega\in\mathcal D$ satisfy $\|\Omega\|=1$, $P^0\Omega=E_\Omega\Omega$ for a real number $E_\Omega$, $P^j\Omega=0$ for $j=1,2,3$, and $\langle P^0\psi,\psi\rangle\ge E_\Omega\|\psi\|^2$ for every $\psi\in D(P^0)$. Say that $\Omega$ is supersymmetry-invariant when $Q^I_\alpha\Omega=(Q^I_\alpha)^*\Omega=0$ for every $I,\alpha$, and supersymmetry-noninvariant when at least one of these vectors is nonzero; say it is boundary-neutral when $Z^{IJ}\Omega=\bar Z_{IJ}\Omega=0$ for every central generator. Then

$$4N E_\Omega=\sum_{I=1}^N\sum_{\alpha=1}^2\left(\|Q^I_\alpha\Omega\|^2+\|(Q^I_\alpha)^*\Omega\|^2\right)\ge0.$$

Consequently, $E_\Omega=0$ if and only if $\Omega$ is supersymmetry-invariant, and every supersymmetry-noninvariant such state has $E_\Omega>0$. The identity holds whether or not the state is boundary-neutral. The energy is an eigenvalue, not an energy density. The theorem is conditional on the representation and state data; it proves neither existence of a vacuum state nor existence of a quantum field theory realizing that representation.

items.title: Exact tree-level minimum in the three-field O’Raifeartaigh model
items.axiom_base: ZF; no choice principle is added by the finite-dimensional minimization argument
items.physical_scope: Exact minimization of the classical canonical F-term scalar potential over pointwise field values for the specified rigid N=1 three-chiral-field Wess–Zumino model. It proves nonzero auxiliary F terms at the pointwise minima but, because the adopted model restricts spacetime fields to compact support, does not identify nonzero constant field values as allowed vacuum configurations. It makes no quantum, radiative-stability, or continuum-QFT claim.

items.design_state: Complete conditional two-regime minimization proof; sources and scoped checks pass; the Wess–Zumino superspace-to-component normalization prerequisite remains owner-escalated.
items.statement:
In the classical rigid N=1 Wess–Zumino model with three chiral scalar coordinates $(\phi_1,\phi_2,\phi_3)\in\mathbb C^3$, canonical Kähler metric, no gauge D-term, and natural units $\hbar=c=1$, adopt the holomorphic superpotential

$$W(\Phi_1,\Phi_2,\Phi_3)=-k\Phi_1+m\Phi_2\Phi_3+\frac y2\Phi_1\Phi_3^2,$$

where $k,m\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$, $y\in\mathbb C$ is arbitrary, and $[\phi_i]=[m]=M$, $[k]=M^2$, and $[y]=1$. The classical zero-derivative F-term potential on pointwise field values is

$$V(\phi_1,\phi_2,\phi_3)=\left|-k+\frac y2\phi_3^2\right|^2+|m\phi_3|^2+|m\phi_2+y\phi_1\phi_3|^2.$$

Here “tree-level” means this classical potential before quantum-loop corrections. At a field value, F-term supersymmetry is unbroken exactly when all eliminated auxiliary fields $F^i=-\overline{\partial_iW}$ vanish; otherwise it is F-term broken.

Put $a=|k|>0$, $b=|m|^2>0$, and $c=|y|$. If $b\ge ac$, including $y=0$, the global minimum is $V_{\min}=a^2=|k|^2$, and all minimizing field values are $\phi_3=\phi_2=0$ with arbitrary $\phi_1\in\mathbb C$. If $0<b<ac$, then $c>0$ and

$$V_{\min}=a^2-\frac{(ac-b)^2}{c^2}=\frac bc\left(2a-\frac bc\right)>0,$$

with all minimizing field values given by arbitrary $\phi_1\in\mathbb C$, one of the two distinct square roots $\phi_3$ of

$$\phi_3^2=\frac{2k}{y}\left(1-\frac{b}{ac}\right),$$

and $\phi_2=-y\phi_1\phi_3/m$. In both regimes every minimizing field value has at least one nonzero auxiliary F term, so the pointwise classical minimum breaks F-term supersymmetry. Thus the stronger bound $V\ge |k|^2$ holds for all field values exactly when $|m|^2\ge |k||y|$; in the other regime the exact minimum is smaller but remains positive. The set of minima has a flat complex $\phi_1$ direction and is not an isolated point. The adopted field-model postulate restricts spacetime fields to compact support, so this pointwise minimization alone does not establish that nonzero constant minimizing values are allowed homogeneous vacuum configurations. No quantum vacuum, stability against radiative corrections, goldstino conclusion, or continuum-QFT existence is asserted.
